Commercial sketch (3-month pilot, 100M tokens/month):

- With recommended batching+caching profile (continuous prefix caching + 32-64 request batching): effective token rate forecast ~ $0.00075 / token (depends on request distribution)
- Quantization impact (for comparable latency targets): 8-bit variant reduces per-token compute cost by ~25%; 4-bit aggressive quant reduces compute cost by ~40% but increases perf risk on long-context chat flows.
- Pilot commercial offer: 30% off baseline for first 3 months + 50k free optimization credits to support tuning (we can convert credits to invoice discount if unused).

Bethany — quick technical appendix below (summarized). I've attached a one-page ops playbook (quant-batching-ops.md).

Summary: caching, batching, and quantization tradeoffs for chat-heavy workloads

- Batching (recommendation): use adaptive batching tuned to your 95th latency SLO. For Brightwell's expected profile (lots of short chat turns, occasional long summaries), set target batch window 12–20ms with a max batch size ~64. This gives 2–3x throughput uplift at tail percentiles while keeping median latency under 140ms on p3-class instances.

- Prefix/KV caching: prefix caching (session-level KV cache) reduces repeated-token compute substantially when users re-use context across turns. If 45–60% of tokens are repeated prefixes, expect 30–45% reduction in compute cost. Implementation notes:
  - Requires routing tokens to the same serving shard for the session or using a distributed KV with affinity keys.
  - Ops effort: ~1–2 engineering sprints to add affinity routing + caching middleware if you don't already have sticky sessions. We can host the cache on our dedicated pool as part of the pilot to remove infra lift from Brightwell.

- Quantization (practical guidance):
  - 8-bit (Q8) is the safe default: ~25% cost reduction, minimal accuracy regressions for instruction-following chat. Works with our preferred kernel set and is a low operational risk.
  - 4-bit (Q4) aggressive: ~40% compute savings but expect occasional decoding artifacts on long-context generation or for retrieval-augmented prompts. If you pick Q4, we recommend a staged rollout: Q8 for canary traffic, Q4 for low-risk background tasks, monitor quality metrics (perplexity, hallucination rate on eval prompts).

- Combined effect: A typical pilot with adaptive batching + prefix caching + Q8 quant yields ~45–55% unit-cost reduction versus the unoptimized baseline. Moving to Q4 may push that to ~60–65% but with the caveats above.

Attachments: quant-batching-ops.md (ops playbook), sample config snippet we can push to your repo if you want. Happy to demo a small synthetic run with your request histogram.

Connor Obrien
Senior ML Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
